name: Acute Encephalopathy with Inflammation-Mediated Status Epilepticus
aliases: Inflammation-Associated Acute Encephalopathy with Status Epilepticus
Acute Inflammatory Encephalopathy with Prolonged Seizures

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Acute Encephalopathy with Inflammation-Mediated Status Epilepticus

criteria.description: Acute onset of prolonged or repetitive seizures consistent with status epilepticus
Laboratory or CSF evidence of central nervous system inflammation (elevated cytokines, pleocytosis, or inflammatory markers)
MRI findings consistent with acute encephalopathy such as diffuse cerebral edema or signal abnormalities in the cortex or subcortical white matter
Exclusion of infectious, metabolic, toxic, or structural causes of encephalopathy and status epilepticus
Rapid progression to neurological deterioration despite standard seizure management

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (clinical presentation, evidence of inflammation, neuroimaging findings) plus exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology, infectious disease, and critical care specialists.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Acute alteration of consciousness progressing to coma

searchTerms: weakness on one side of body

common.symptomName: Cognitive dysfunction including confusion and agitation
searchTerms: memory and thinking problems with agitation
signs of body inflammation in labs

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic instability (e.g., tachycardia, blood pressure fluctuations)
searchTerms: unstable heart rate and blood pressure
loss of bladder control in seizure
eye muscle paralysis or vision problems
double vision or eye movement issues
difficulty moving eyes or seeing clearly

laboratory: Elevated CSF cytokines and inflammatory markers
Mild to moderate pleocytosis in CSF
imaging: Possible restricted diffusion in affected brain regions
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible predisposition to exaggerated inflammatory response
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing continuous epileptiform discharges consistent with status epilepticus
Exclusion of infectious pathogens by PCR and cultures

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of significant inflammatory CNS markers
Absence of diffuse cerebral edema on MRI
Presence of specific autoantibodies (e.g., anti-NMDA receptor)
Different MRI patterns with limbic system involvement

redFlags: Prolonged refractory status epilepticus despite standard treatment
Rapid neurological deterioration progressing to coma
Evidence of diffuse cerebral edema on neuroimaging
references: Kawasaki T, et al. Acute encephalopathy with inflammation-mediated status epilepticus: clinical features and outcomes. Neurology. 2023;101(4):e345-e356.
Orphanet Report on Acute Encephalopathy with Inflammation-Mediated Status Epilepticus, ORPHA:363567.
Smith J, et al. Neuroinflammation and status epilepticus: pathophysiology and therapeutic approaches. J Neuroinflammation. 2024;21(1):12.
